# 🔒 Security Policy

## 📅 Supported Versions

| Version | Supported          |
|---------|--------------------|
| 1.0.x   | ✅ Active development |

## 🚨 Reporting a Vulnerability

**⚠️ Do NOT report security vulnerabilities in public GitHub issues.**

NexKey Keyboard takes security seriously. Although the app makes zero network
calls and stores all data on-device, we still appreciate responsible disclosure.

### 🔒 Private Reporting Process

1. 🔗 Go to [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/abir2afridi/NexKey-Keyboard/security/advisories/new).
2. 📋 Click **"Report a vulnerability"**.
3. ✏️ Fill in the details, including:
   - 📝 Description of the vulnerability
   - 📋 Steps to reproduce
   - 💥 Potential impact
   - 🔧 Suggested fix (if any)

### ⏳ What to Expect

- 📬 **Acknowledgment**: Within 48 hours of submission.
- 📅 **Initial assessment**: Within 5 business days.
- 🎯 **Resolution target**: Critical issues within 7 days, high within 14 days.
- 📢 **Disclosure**: We will coordinate disclosure timing with you.

## 🌍 Scope

### ✅ In Scope
- 📱 NexKey Keyboard APK (all versions)
- ⌨️ IME service behavior and data handling
- 📋 Clipboard manager data persistence
- 💾 Room database (learned words, clipboard history)
- 🔔 Permission handling (RECORD_AUDIO, VIBRATE, POST_NOTIFICATIONS)
- 🔒 Password field detection and incognito mode

### ❌ Out of Scope
- 📦 Third-party libraries (report to their respective maintainers)
- 🤖 Android OS / AOSP vulnerabilities
- 📱 Physical device security
- 🕵️ Social engineering attacks

## 🛡️ Safe Harbor

We consider security research conducted under this policy as:

- ✅ Authorized under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA) and similar laws
- ✅ Exempt from DMCA anti-circumvention provisions
- ✅ Not a violation of our Acceptable Use Policy

We will not pursue legal action against researchers who:

- 📝 Follow this disclosure policy
- 🙏 Make a good faith effort to avoid privacy violations
- 💥 Do not destroy or corrupt data
- 🔒 Do not publicly disclose the vulnerability before it is fixed

## 🔐 Preferred Encryption

We do not currently support PGP key submission. Please use GitHub Security
Advisories for all security-related communications.
